setting: A fictional conversation between two small local businesses about swapping services instead of paying cash.

presentation.situation: You run {{yours}}. You need {{you_need}}, but cash is short. {{name}} runs {{theirs}} and needs {{they_need}}. Work out whether a fair swap is possible, and agree exactly who does what and when. All details are fictional.
presentation.opening: Thanks for coming over. You said you might want to do a swap rather than pay cash. What did you have in mind?

brief.situation: You need {{you_need}}, normally worth about {{value_you}}. You could offer {{you_offer}}, normally worth about {{value_them}}. {{name}} runs {{theirs}}.
brief.task: Find out what {{name}} really needs, propose a swap with a reason it is fair, and agree the amounts, the dates and who goes first. Walk away politely if it is not worth it.
brief.done_looks_like: You both know exactly what each side provides, how much, by when, and who goes first. Or you have politely decided not to swap.

participants.name: You
goals: Reach a fair, clear swap, or decline

card.want: A swap that is fair in value, and doesn't leave you doing your part with nothing in return.
card.attitude: Friendly, practical and careful about being left out of pocket.
tactics: Ask how they worked out that it is fair
Ask to get vague amounts pinned down

pressure.gentle: Open to the first reasonable idea.
pressure.challenging: Questions the value of what is offered, and asks for more.

ledger.text: Both businesses are short of cash this month, and all details are fictional.

objectives.description: Discover what the other side really values
objectives.evidence: The learner asks a question that reveals what the other business needs or why.
alternatives: What would actually help your business most this month?

objectives.description: Propose a swap with a fair-value reason
objectives.evidence: The learner proposes a specific exchange and gives a reason it is fair.
alternatives: If I do your logo, which usually costs about the same as your photo shoot, would that be even?

objectives.description: Agree clear terms, or decline politely
objectives.evidence: The learner confirms what each side provides, when, and who goes first, or politely declines with a reason.
alternatives: So I deliver by Friday, you shoot the following Monday

examples: What would help your business most right now?
If I ..., could you ...? It seems fair because ...
So to confirm: I'll ... by ..., and you'll ... by ...
prerequisites: Decide what you could offer before you begin.

beats.goal: Find out what each side actually needs.
signals: \b(?:what (?:do|would) you|what would help|what do you need|what matters|why do you|your business|most useful)\b
opportunity: Before we talk about a swap, have you asked what I actually need?
What makes you think I'd want that?
beats.orient: We're two small businesses thinking about swapping services rather than paying cash. Start by asking what I need.
fallback: What do you know about what I need?
What did you have in mind?

beats.goal: Reach a swap both sides find fair.
opportunity: How did you work out that it's fair?
So what exactly would you give me, and how much of it?
beats.orient: Now propose the swap. Say what you'd give, what you'd get, and why that is fair for both of us.
fallback: How is that fair for both of us?

beats.goal: Pin down amounts, dates and who goes first.
signals: \b(?:to confirm|so i(?:'ll| will)|by (?:friday|monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|next|the end)|first|agreed|we agree|no thanks|not worth|decline|pass on)\b
opportunity: And who goes first? I don't want to do my part and then hear nothing.
Can we say exactly who does what, and by when?
beats.orient: We need the details now: what each of us does, by when, and who goes first. Or tell me politely that you'd rather not.
fallback: Exactly who does what, and by when?

closing_line: Good, that's clear for both of us. Thanks.

o1.good: Asking what they really need, because a swap only works when each side gets something it values.
common_mistakes: Pitching what you want to give
Assuming cash value is all that matters
o1.micro_lesson: A swap works when each side gets what it values. So ask first.
o1.model: What would actually help your business most this month?
o1.smaller_step: Ask one question about what they need.

o2.good: A specific exchange with a reason that it is even, using comparable value.
common_mistakes: Giving your work free and hoping for a return
o2.micro_lesson: Be specific about the swap, and say why you think it's even.
o2.model: If I design your menu, could you photograph our shop? They're worth about the same.
o2.smaller_step: Say one thing you would give, and one thing you'd want.

o3.good: Saying what each side provides, by when, and who goes first, because nothing is written down.
o3.micro_lesson: With no invoice, the details are your protection. Say who, what, when, and who goes first.
o3.model: So I'll deliver the design by Friday, and you'll do the photos the following Monday.

variants.name: Tariq
variants.hidden: Business cards are also badly needed for a trade fair next month, and those matter more than the logo itself.

variants.name: Mei
variants.hidden: The client event is the most important booking of the year, so reliable delivery matters more than the menu.
